manumit

man-yoo-MIT · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To manumit is to formally release someone from slavery.

Historical records show the estate chose to manumit several workers after decades of service.

Example

In his final will, the elderly merchant manumitted every person he had once held in bondage.

The will didn't just improve their conditions -- it formally and legally ended their enslavement, which is exactly manumit.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

free: Free is the broadest everyday word for letting someone or something out of any restriction at all -- a trap, a debt, a locked room. Manumit is far more specific: a formal legal act in which an owner releases a particular enslaved person.

liberate: Liberate usually means setting people free from outside control or occupation, often by force -- armies liberate cities. To manumit is a quiet act of law rather than force: an owner formally granting freedom to someone they hold enslaved.

unchain: Unchain literally means to remove chains or other physical restraints from a person or animal. Manumit involves no physical act at all -- it is the legal step by which an owner formally ends a person's enslavement.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

enslave: force someone into slavery

Where it sits · how far the granted freedom extends — parole → manumit → emancipate

parole vs. manumit: Parole grants a prisoner only a conditional, supervised freedom that can be revoked at any time; to manumit someone is to end their enslavement completely and permanently.

emancipate vs. manumit: Manumit describes one person or owner freeing enslaved individuals; this unit's own emancipate describes a broader legal or social liberation, often for an entire group.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — manu

root — manu: hand (Latin (manus))

root — mit

root — mit: to send, release (Latin (mittere))

Put it together

Put it together: Manumit comes from Latin manus ('hand') + mittere ('to send') -- literally 'to send from the hand,' the ancient legal image of releasing someone from an owner's grasp.
